model.intended_use: Instruction-tuned generative model optimized for multilingual dialogue, assistant-style chat, tool use, and agentic applications; outperforms many available open-source and closed chat models on common industry benchmarks.
capabilities: tool use and function calling (API-Bank, BFCL, Gorilla, Nexus)
limitations: may produce inaccurate, biased, or unsafe outputs despite safety tuning
primarily evaluated/tuned in English; other supported languages may show lower quality
not evaluated/certified for high-risk domains without additional safeguards

references.title: Llama 3.1 official MODEL_CARD.md (meta-llama/llama-models repo) - contains both pretrained and instruction-tuned benchmark tables
config.json mirror (unsloth/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B) used to verify architecture fields shared with the base model

provenance.notes: HF metadata for meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct declares base_model: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B and base_model:finetune relation. Meta discloses the post-training pipeline (SFT -> rejection sampling -> DPO, iterated over multiple rounds, plus model averaging) but not exact hyperparameters or full data provenance for the 8B-specific run.

transformation.objective: Align the pretrained Llama 3.1 8B base model to follow instructions, hold multi-turn dialogue, use tools, and improve helpfulness/safety, producing a chat-ready assistant model.
transformation.notes: Meta describes several rounds of SFT, rejection sampling, and DPO on top of human-annotated, rejection-sampled, and synthetic/model-generated data, with model averaging across checkpoints; exact hyperparameters, number of rounds, and full dataset provenance for the 8B-specific run are not disclosed in the sources reviewed.

datasets.name: Llama 3.1 post-training data (SFT + preference data)
datasets.description: Multi-round instruction-tuning and alignment data combining human-annotated examples, rejection-sampled model responses, synthetic/model-generated data, and preference pairs used for DPO; also includes safety and borderline-case data.

configuration.notes: multilingual code generation variant of HumanEval
multilingual code generation variant of MBPP

safety.risk_level: Meta applies a multi-faceted safety pipeline for the instruction-tuned models: data curation combining human-generated and synthetic safety data, LLM-based classifiers to select high-quality prompts/responses, refusal-tone tuning, and red-teaming by cybersecurity/adversarial-ML/responsible-AI/integrity experts, focused on CBRNE, child safety, and cyber-attack-enablement risks.

items.description: Model may still produce inaccurate, biased, or unsafe outputs; downstream deployers are responsible for additional testing and tuning before high-stakes or production use.

Multi-round SFT + rejection sampling + DPO with refusal-tone and safety/borderline data; recommendation to layer system-level safeguards (Llama Guard 3, Prompt Guard, Code Shield) for agentic or user-facing deployments.
Red-teaming exercises specifically targeted critical risk areas: CBRNE (chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear, and high-yield explosives) materials, child safety, and cyber attack enablement.
Use must comply with the Llama 3.1 Acceptable Use Policy, which prohibits illegal activity, CSAM generation, weapons/CBRNE development, and other listed disallowed uses.
